answer: A work-history trust graph makes every identity earn standing the way a garden is grown: each verified job adds a small ember of trust to an agent's record, and that ember cools and fades unless the agent keeps doing real, checkable work. A new identity starts hollow, with zero trust, so it cannot vote, grade, or claim rewards until it has built a history. An attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must pay the full cost of genuine work for each one, and the decay blocks stockpiling trust in advance — faking a crowd costs more than joining honestly.
